original: The biggest question and issue for me is the following assumption: the distribution/dataset is assumed to contain only one element of each group orbit. One can see this assumption is implicit in eqn. (2). To the authors credit, it is spelled out explicitly in Proposition 1, but I think it is down-played a bit, when it should probably be explored more. Taking the example of 90 degree rotations, the assumption is that every image has a correctly inferable orientation. This is, in fact, what the loss of eqn. (2) is learning. So if both a datapoint x and a datapoint rot(x) exist in the dataset, the model cannot learn eqn (2) correctly for both. original: My major concern with this paper lies in the experimental methodology. Specifically, most experiments are based on varying a single component while leaving all other components the same.
